topic: What Would Happen If There Were No Wheels in the World?

beats.narration: If every wheel on Earth vanished tonight, you wouldn't make it to work tomorrow... and that's the least of your problems.

shots.scene_description: Stylized 3D man in a blue hoodie holding car keys, staring in shock at his red hatchback car whose four wheels are dissolving into glowing particles, suburban driveway at dawn.
Close-up of the red hatchback car body slamming down onto the asphalt where its wheel used to be, sparks and dust bursting out.

beats.narration: First, every car, bus and train drops straight onto its axles, freezing every highway into one giant parking lot.

shots.scene_description: Aerial view of a huge multi-lane highway full of cars, buses and trucks all lying flat on the road with no wheels, completely frozen.
Cross-section cutaway of a train with no wheels, its steel axles grinding directly on the rail track, sparks flying.

beats.narration: But it's not just vehicles. Inside your watch, your engine, and every power plant, gears are just wheels with teeth.

shots.scene_description: Cutaway view inside a wristwatch showing tiny golden gears, the gears beginning to vanish one by one.
Transparent cutaway of a car engine and gearbox with glowing interlocking gears disappearing, leaving empty shafts.

beats.narration: So the turbines stop spinning, and the power grid collapses. Lights out, across the entire planet.

shots.scene_description: Cutaway of a power plant turbine hall, the giant turbine wheel grinding to a halt, warning lights flashing red.
Night view of Earth from space, city lights across the continents blinking out in a wave until the planet is dark.

beats.narration: Without trucks, supermarket shelves would be empty in about three days, because food simply can't move fast enough.

shots.scene_description: A delivery truck lying flat on a highway with no wheels, crates of fruit and vegetables spilling out the back.
The man in the blue hoodie standing alone in a supermarket aisle with completely empty shelves, holding an empty basket.

beats.narration: Planes are grounded too. No landing gear to take off, and no spinning turbines inside the jet engines.

shots.scene_description: A passenger jet lying on its belly on the runway with no landing gear wheels, scraped and stuck.
Cross-section cutaway of a jet engine, its spinning fan and turbine discs vanishing, the engine going cold and silent.

beats.narration: So we'd go back to moving heavy things the ancient way: dragging them on sledges with ropes and muscle.

shots.scene_description: The man in the blue hoodie straining to pull a wooden sledge piled with groceries and a fridge along a city street with ropes.
Close-up of the wooden sledge runners scraping and digging into the asphalt, wood splintering.

beats.narration: But here's the crazy part. Humans lived for hundreds of thousands of years without the wheel. It was only invented about 5,500 years ago... and not for carts.

shots.scene_description: Stylized 3D ancient Mesopotamian village by a river at golden hour, mud brick houses, people carrying baskets by hand.
A glowing timeline floating in the air, ancient clay tablets and a question mark hovering over an empty spot.

beats.narration: It was for making pottery. Which means if wheels disappeared, someone would probably reinvent them within a week.

shots.scene_description: Ancient potter's hands shaping a clay pot on a spinning stone potter's wheel, wet clay glistening.
The man in the blue hoodie in his garage proudly holding up a freshly carved round wooden wheel, a lightbulb glowing above his head.

beats.narration: Because the wheel isn't just an invention. It's the thing quietly holding the modern world together.

shots.scene_description: Wheels rematerializing in glowing light under the red hatchback car, the car lifting back up off the asphalt.
Busy modern city at sunset with cars, trains, bikes and wind turbines all spinning and moving again, city lights switching back on.
